events.factual_description: Totsuka Civic Cultural Center Sakura Plaza presents UNPLUGGED Keiichiro Shibuya + Naruyoshi Kikuchi on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Doors open at 18:00 and the approximately 120-minute performance begins at 18:30, with an intermission. Sakura Plaza states that Shibuya and Kikuchi will perform works from their respective catalogs and play together in session, and that a newly written work is planned. The presenter identifies this as the first performance by the pair in this configuration since 2017, a gap of nine years. The announced ticket categories are ¥3,000 general, ¥2,500 Yokohama resident, ¥1,500 EX limited-view/auxiliary seating, and ¥1,000 student.

priority_review.rationale: Concrete scarcity: Sakura Plaza states that Keiichiro Shibuya and Naruyoshi Kikuchi have not performed in this piano-saxophone configuration since 2017, making the October 17 engagement a nine-year reunion, and the presenter also states that a newly written work is planned for this one-night program. A+ would understate the genuine-regret-if-missed character of missing the only announced Kanto reunion date when a stay overlaps it. S+ would overstate the claim because the performance is rare and newly created, but not a documented farewell or historically singular milestone.

en.why_it_matters: This is not just two versatile Japanese musicians sharing a bill. Shibuya and Kikuchi are stripping the encounter down to piano and saxophone, returning to a duo configuration they have not used together since 2017, and Sakura Plaza says a newly written work is planned. That makes the night about friction and space between two very different musical languages: Shibuya's composition-and-technology world reduced to the physical piano, and Kikuchi's saxophone voice meeting it without a larger ensemble to absorb the collision.
en.trip_verdict: If a Tokyo/Kanto stay overlaps October 17, protect the evening and go to Totsuka rather than treating Yokohama as an optional add-on. The nine-year gap and planned new work make this the kind of Kanto date worth building the night around.

es.why_it_matters: No es simplemente un cartel con dos músicos japoneses muy versátiles. Shibuya y Kikuchi reducen el encuentro a piano y saxofón, vuelven a una formación que no compartían desde 2017 y Sakura Plaza anuncia que planean presentar una obra nueva. Eso pone el peso de la noche en el roce y el espacio entre dos lenguajes muy distintos: el mundo de composición y tecnología de Shibuya llevado al piano físico, frente al saxofón de Kikuchi sin una banda grande que amortigüe el choque.
es.trip_verdict: Si una estancia en Tokio/Kanto coincide con el 17 de octubre, protegería la noche y me movería hasta Totsuka en vez de tratar Yokohama como un desvío opcional. Nueve años sin esta formación y una obra nueva planeada hacen que valga construir la velada alrededor de esta fecha.
